AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Lifestyle factors, such as diet, body weight, and physical activity, are linked to better survival after breast cancer (BC) diagnosis. A high percentage of the Malaysian population is overweight or obese. In addition, studies have shown a disparity in survival among Malaysian women compared with other higher-income countries. The Malaysian Breast Cancer Survivorship Cohort (MyBCC) study aims to study lifestyle factors that affect survival in BC survivors. These are the preliminary findings on the nutritional status of Malaysian BC survivors.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Our aim was to evaluate the nutritional status of BC survivors at 1 year after diagnosis.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: This was a cross-sectional study of 194 participants from the MyBCC study, recruited within 1 year of their diagnosis. Participants completed a 3-day food diary.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: Malaysian women (aged 18 years and older) who were newly diagnosed with primary BC, managed at the University Malaya Medical Center, and able to converse either in Malay, English, or Mandarin were included.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: Dietary intake and prevalence of overweight or obesity among participants 1 year after diagnosis were measured.

AbstractText.Label: STATISTICAL ANALYSES PERFORMED
AbstractText.content: Student's t test and analysis of variance or its equivalent nonparametric test were used for association in continuous variables.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: About 66% (n=129) of participants were overweight or obese and >45% (n=86) had high body fat percentage 1 year after diagnosis. The participants' diets were low in fiber (median=8.7 g/day; interquartile range=7.2 g/day) and calcium (median=458 mg/day; interquartile range=252 mg/day). Ethnicity and educational attainment contributed to the differences in dietary intake among participants. Higher saturated fat and lower fiber intake were observed among Malay participants compared with other ethnic groups.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Overweight and obesity were highly prevalent among BC survivors and suboptimal dietary intake was observed. Provision of an individualized medical nutrition therapy by a qualified dietitian is crucial as part of comprehensive BC survivorship care.

Article.ArticleTitle: Nutritional Status of Breast Cancer Survivors 1 Year after Diagnosis: A Preliminary Analysis from the Malaysian Breast Cancer Survivorship Cohort Study.

Journal.Title: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics

Keyword.content: Malaysian Breast Cancer Survivorship Cohort (MyBCC) study
